newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST - HUNGARY GOVT BOND YIELDS SEEN STEADY.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - HUNGARY GOVT BOND YIELDS SEEN STEADY.

text.p: Government securities yields on Hungary's secondary market are seen changing little this week after last week's sharp falls, traders said on Monday.

"I think (the yields) will remain unchanged this week, unless there is strong demand at the (Friday) auction of 12-month T-bills," said Csaba Keresztyen of K&H Broker. "In that case one-year papers will drop a little."

Traders said the yields on government bonds with one- to three-year maturities dropped by about one percentage point last week, mainly due to low yields set at the Thursday auctions of five-year and two-year government bonds.
The average yield on the five-year bonds was set at 15.69 percent while that for two-year bonds was fixed at 18.58 percent.
One-year bonds currently trade on the secondary market at yields of around 20 percent, two-year bonds at about 19 percent and three-year bonds at between 18.3 and 18.7 percent.

Traders said market liquidity -- boosted by the maturity of a series of bonds worth 30 billion forints, interest payments on other bonds, and other factors -- strengthened demand for government bonds at last week's auctions.

Recent suggestions by the government that Hungary may reduce the monthly 1.2 percent rate of its pre-announced crawling-peg devaluations ahead of the previously planned date of July 1 also boosted demand for the bonds, traders said.
But these factors have already been built into prices and this week was not likely to bring any significant change, traders added.
